news.title: Telford football referee returns from 'incredible' China tournament
news.lede: A young football referee who has just returned from officiating at a world schools tournament in China has said it was a "scary" but also "incredible" experience. Callum Oram, 18, has been refereeing for three years and hopes to make it his full time career. He spent 11 days working at the International School Sport Federation Football World Cup in Suzhou and made friends with other young referees from around the world. The Telford College student said he believed the tournament would be a valuable learning experience and would help him move ahead in the game.

news.title: FIFA politics around Infantino re-election push Japanese official to resign
news.lede: GENEVA (AP) — Two-time World Cup coach Takeshi Okada resigned as Japanese soccer federation vice president in protest at the politics around FIFA during Gianni Infantino's campaign to be re-elected. Japan's soccer body on Wednesday published Okada's resignation statement dated last Saturday — 24 hours after the Asian Football Confederation had performed a U-turn by publicly supporting Infantino, who seeks a fourth and final presidential term at an election in March. Infantino has faced a backlash since July over his failed World Cup sell-off plan and broader management style including ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, provoking a furor from soccer leaders in Europe, North America and — initially — in Asia.

news.title: Japan football vice president Okada quits over FIFA World Cup decisions
news.lede: Takeshi Okada, vice president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), resigned on Wednesday, stating that the organization’s "series of responses" to recent World Cup controversies conflicted with his personal values. Okada, who led Japan as head coach at the 1998 and 2010 World Cups, stepped down a week after Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa declared the region's full support for Gianni Infantino’s FIFA re-election bid during a meeting in Tokyo. The AFC's endorsement marked a shift coming just weeks after joining European and North American governing bodies in criticizing Infantino over plans to open major FIFA competitions to private investors. Infantino continues to face pressure over governance decisions as continental associations debate his leadership tenure.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Former Japan coach Okada quits JFA vice-president role over FIFA concerns
news.lede: Oct 28 (Reuters) - Former Japan ⁠coach Takeshi Okada has resigned as vice-president of the ⁠Japan Football Association, citing concerns over developments surrounding FIFA and ‌the World Cup, the JFA said on Wednesday. Okada's resignation came a week after Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa declared support for ​Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as ⁠FIFA president at the AFC's ⁠extraordinary congress in Tokyo. The endorsement marked a sharp shift from the ⁠AFC's ‌position three months earlier, when the confederation accused FIFA of a "fundamental breach of trust" over the abandoned FIFA ⁠Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal to sell a stake in ​FIFA competitions. "Guided by ‌my belief that sports should embody integrity, I have always ⁠valued their ​social significance," Okada said in a statement on theJFA website.
